rationale: The current topology suffers from poor noise figure and insufficient gain, with the most negative margins in NF (−0.627) and S21 (−1.03). The primary issue stems from inadequate transconductance and improper impedance matching due to the lack of a proper inductive degeneration or load network. Adding a source inductor to M1 (the input transistor) will improve both noise figure and gain by increasing the effective input impedance and enhancing the transconductance-to-noise ratio, while maintaining stability. This is a standard technique in low-noise amplifier design for 45nm CMOS to achieve high gain with low NF, particularly in narrowband applications like 2.44 GHz WiFi. The inductor provides a resonant load at f0, improving gain and matching without adding significant power overhead.
